response.text: Consumer fireworks may generally be discharged in the City only on Victoria Day or Canada Day, or on a day for which a special occasions fireworks discharge permit has been applied for and issued by the Fire Chief [2]. If weather makes the designated day impractical or unsafe, the next day before or after applies [2]. On those designated days, discharge is not allowed after 11:00 p.m. [2]. You may not discharge consumer fireworks on land you do not own unless the owner has given prior written consent, and you must have fire extinguishing equipment ready at the site [2]. Discharge is also prohibited within 100 metres of certain institutions such as hospitals, schools and religious institutions, unless the owner or authorized representative consents [3]. A fireworks discharge permit is not required for consumer fireworks on Victoria Day or Canada Day [1]. The passages do not cover whether a backyard is considered land you own for these purposes beyond the consent rule stated.
